title: The deadly forces behind Nepal’s Himalayan disasters
content: In Langtang National Park, a large ice and rock collapse triggered a severe flooding incident, revealing Nepal's ongoing struggle with natural disasters intensified by climate change. Rapid urban growth and human activities exacerbate exposure to these perilous weather events. Although the government has taken steps to bolster disaster management, glaring weaknesses in early warning systems persist. To better manage risks, the country must focus on improved monitoring and stronger infrastructure.

title: ‘I urge others to speak up’: Ex-Pak cricketer's emotional appeal for Imran Khan
content: Moin Khan urges authorities to honour Imran Khan's right to medical care. He also asked fellow cricketers to voice their support for the former leader. International captains have also called for adequate healthcare and constitutional safeguards. Greg Chappell described Imran Khan's condition as worrying and difficult to ascertain. The Pakistan Cricket Board lodged a complaint after an interview with Imran Khan's sons aired.

title: From making iPhones to building the next Apple: Will India's Rs 62K-cr bet pay off?
content: With the launch of the Rs 62,500 crore Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS), India is eyeing its homegrown smartphone brands - with every aspect from design, R&D to components and manufacturing taking place in the country.

title: Jamie Dimon says it is ‘frustrating’ to hear America is behind in defence tech
content: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon voiced frustration regarding US defense technology perceptions.  The bank launched a $1.5 trillion Security and Resiliency Initiative for national security industries.  This program now includes Canada, Europe, and the United Kingdom.  The initiative supports aerospace, defense, manufacturing, energy, and health tech sectors.  The bank is investing significant capital and personnel into this critical effort.

title: H-1B workers' 60-day grace period may end: What happens next
content: The US Department of Homeland Security is considering a proposal that may eliminate the 60-day grace period for foreign workers, particularly affecting H-1B visa holders and countless Indian professionals. This grace period currently allows individuals to seek new jobs or modify their status before needing to leave the US. Without it in place, workers may face immediate departure following job loss, with final details pending further evaluation.

title: Minnesota removed common carp; lake clarity rose nearly 600% afterward
content: Pickerel Lake, Minnesota, has battled significant water quality and algal bloom problems for decades, primarily due to invasive common carp taking over the shallow waters. After their removal in 2009, the lake underwent a remarkable ecological revival, with water clarity significantly improving and native aquatic plants flourishing once more. This successful restoration highlights the pivotal role of addressing invasive species in revitalizing ecosystems.

title: Houston lawyer buys $15.5M mansion to demolish it for a garden
content: In River Oaks, Houston lawyer Tony Buzbee has bought a mansion primarily for property expansion. Teaming up with Habitat for Humanity, he aims to salvage valuable construction materials, which will provide substantial support—millions of pounds worth—for affordable housing projects. The planned demolition will allow for the development of a larger private garden estate while enhancing his family's legacy through philanthropic efforts.

title: Elon Musk breaks silence on OpenAI cutting 3-year-old deal with Cursor over him
content: OpenAI has officially announced the termination of its collaboration with Cursor, recently acquired by SpaceX under Elon Musk. This unexpected decision follows claims of contract infractions associated with Musk's enterprises, notably Twitter and xAI. OpenAI has expressed concerns about SpaceX's adherence to its service terms, resulting in Cursor losing model access by November 2026. Meanwhile, discussions are underway between SpaceX and OpenAI to find a resolution to the ongoing conflict.

title: A film studio for Meghan, privacy for Harry: Inside the Sussexes' UK home search
content: Meghan Markle and Prince Harry are reportedly house-hunting in the Cotswolds for a new home.  They seek a large country estate with many bedrooms and private land.  The couple arrived in the UK and are staying with a wealthy friend.  Their children, Archie and Lili, are expected to attend a local prep school.  The family plans to base themselves in the UK during school terms.

title: Flood fears in Bihar as several rivers cross danger marks amid Nepal rains
content: Bihar faces intensified flood fears as river water levels rise significantly. Persistent rains in Nepal and the state have caused rivers to exceed danger marks. The Gandak river has breached its danger level, releasing substantial water downstream. Authorities have moved residents from low-lying areas and placed departments on alert. District magistrates are personally monitoring the escalating flood situation across vulnerable regions.

title: How a Wimbledon upset of Venus Williams became Coco Gauff’s turning point?
content: Coco Gauff's stunning victory over Venus Williams at Wimbledon in 2019 marked a pivotal moment in her career, transforming her from an aspiring junior player into a recognized name in global tennis. This win acted as a springboard for her outstanding accomplishments, culminating in a Grand Slam title in 2023.

title: What does Tom Brady keep from every Super Bowl win? The answer is on his phone
content: Tom Brady has seven Super Bowl rings, but one of his most personal collections lives on his phone. The former NFL quarterback revealed that he created separate folders for his championship victories and saved congratulatory messages sent after each one. The habit has preserved a private record of a career that included 10 Super Bowl appearances and five Super Bowl MVP awards.

title: Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims recall narrow escape from Nepal floods
content: Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims encountered life-threatening flash floods in Nepal's Rasuwa Bhote Koshi area, leading to a catastrophic toll of 675 confirmed casualties and 2,418 individuals missing. In response, India is playing a pivotal role in humanitarian efforts, dispatching technical teams to evaluate flood-affected hydropower tunnels and providing more than 57 tonnes of crucial emergency supplies to assist ongoing rescue operations.

title: Women’s Hockey WC: Argentina stun Netherlands in shootout to win third title
content: Argentina's women's hockey team secured a remarkable World Cup victory on Saturday. They defeated the top-ranked Netherlands team in a thrilling final match. Goalkeeper Cristina Cosentino was instrumental in the team's stunning upset win. Argentina clinched their third World Cup title after a tense shoot-out. Belgium secured third place by beating Australia in their match.

title: 4 injured as helium balloons explode during Velankanni festival in TN
content: The annual feast of St. Mary's Nativity commenced in Velankanni with a flag hoisting ceremony.  Four devotees sustained injuries when helium balloons exploded near the church.  Thousands of devotees gathered for the event, which began with a procession.  Special masses and a holy car procession are scheduled during the eleven-day celebration.  Over a million devotees are expected to visit the shrine during this period.

title: Flood scare in MP: IAF helicopters, SDRF teams deployed as Mandakini river overflows
content: Indian Air Force helicopters were deployed to rescue stranded people in Chitrakoot. Torrential rains caused the Mandakini river to overflow, flooding large parts of the town. Three State Disaster Response Force teams were also engaged in shifting people to safer places. A dam breach in Uttar Pradesh worsened the situation, while relief shelters were prepared. The water level in the Mandakini had started receding Saturday night after rainfall paused.

title: ‘He could be in the realms of Lara and Tendulkar’: Boycott’s big Brook warning
content: Sir Geoffrey Boycott has high praise for Harry Brook's exceptional batting skills but expresses concern that Brook isn't fully harnessing his potential in Test cricket. He believes Brook's style is too reminiscent of white-ball play, suggesting it could hinder his development. Boycott sees similarities between Brook and legendary players like Lara and Tendulkar but laments that his advice went unheeded.

title: Nepal flash floods: How a tea break saved lives of 5 Chhattisgarh friends
content: Five friends from Raipur found themselves in a life-threatening situation in Nepal when they narrowly escaped flash floods. A timely tea break allowed them to stay clear of the destruction caused by the surging Trishuli river, which swept away vehicles and debris. Huddled in safety for two anxious days, they eventually returned home without harm, relieved and thankful.

title: John Cena reveals he and The Rock ‘hated each other’ before WrestleMania showdown
content: John Cena openly acknowledged the animosity that brewed before his WrestleMania 28 clash with The Rock. Their competitive rivalry escalated beyond the ring, leading to personal jabs and near confrontations backstage during heated promo exchanges. Although Cena publicly insisted he would prevail, he privately recognized The Rock's impending victory. After the match, heartfelt apologies paved the way for a newfound respect between the two icons.

title: ‘A little jealous’: Sunil Chhetri on India’s chance to play Brazil, Uruguay
content: Sunil Chhetri, the revered former captain, expresses a nuanced envy as he observes the current Indian football team gearing up for matches against legendary opponents like Brazil and Uruguay. He emphasises the importance of these unique encounters and encourages young players to make the most of this chance. Chhetri has confidence in the coach's choices and urges a united front for a brighter future in Indian football.

title: Trump vs Carney: Cars, homes, booze and more caught in US-Canada tariff war
content: The recent imposition of new tariffs on vehicles and construction materials has intensified the trade conflict between the US and Canada. This has also led to surging import taxes on other household products and alcoholic beverages. Both businesses and consumers are likely to feel the pinch with escalating costs, potentially affecting employment rates. Moreover, these disputes cast a shadow of uncertainty over the USMCA trade agreement.

title: Fuel paradox: Russia has oil, so why is it importing petrol from India?
content: Russian petrol stations are rationing fuel due to Ukrainian drone attacks on refineries.  These strikes have disrupted domestic fuel supplies, causing shortages across the nation.  Russia is now importing finished petrol from countries like India to meet demand.  This unusual trade flow highlights the difference between crude production and refining capacity.  The ongoing refinery damage strains Russia's energy system supporting its economy.

title: ‘I am the king’: Ex-cricketer reveals how Ganguly transformed Team India’s mindset
content: Deep Dasgupta, the former Indian cricketer, emphasised the profound influence of Sourav Ganguly on the team's culture. Ganguly's commanding 'I am the king' mindset instilled confidence, encouraging players to stand up to sledging. This pivotal shift fostered a new combative spirit within the Indian cricket team, leading to notable victories both at home and abroad during his captaincy.

title: Rebuilding after devastating floods may cost Nepal nearly 10% of its economy
content: Nepal's finance minister estimates flood reconstruction costs between four and five billion dollars.  This devastating flood killed over 600 people and left thousands missing.  The disaster destroyed towns, bridges, roads, and damaged hydropower stations significantly.  Search and rescue operations continue despite disruptions from bad weather conditions.  India has provided substantial relief materials to the affected regions.

title: After Bombay HC rap, FDA withdraws orders against Cipla, MCA eateries
content: The Bombay High Court took a firm stance against the Maharashtra FDA, rebuking its treatment of Cipla and five eateries. The court underscored that the FDA's decisions compromised natural justice and displayed an inflexible approach. With the court's direction, the FDA rescinded its suspension of the Mumbai Cricket Association restaurants and reinstated Cipla's drug sale licence. The court called on the FDA to practice due diligence in its enforcement strategies.

title: Karnataka HC slams cops over activist’s ‘illegal arrest’ in Kunal Kamra show cancellation

Noting a pattern of procedural violations at the station, the court highlighted that the activist was apprehended following a Facebook post celebrating a canceled show. The police initiated action under a suo motu case, lacking a formal complaint, prompting authorities to demand clarifications on these irregularities.

title: BFSI firms drive India’s GCC office leasing as demand shifts beyond tech

Conversely, foreign IT-ITeS firms have cut back on office space absorption. The commercial real estate market in India reflects changing dynamics, with other service and manufacturing sectors displaying distinct trends in their leasing decisions.

title: 'Grateful for special gesture': PM Modi thanks Uzbek prez for warm welcome

Modi will then attend the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit in Bishkek. This visit aims to strengthen India's strategic partnerships in Central Asia. The summit will bring together leaders from ten member nations.

title: UP woman threatens to end life by jumping into river, passerby saves her
content: A woman threatened to jump from Pakka Pul bridge over the Gomti River. She reached the bridge after an argument with her family members. Police arrived and attempted to persuade her to step away from the railing. A passerby intervened and successfully pulled her away from the edge. The incident, stemming from a family dispute, was resolved safely.

title: FSSAI bans sale of hing powder by Everest, Laljee Godhoo over sub-standard quality
content: India's food safety authority, FSSAI, has taken a significant step by banning the sales of hing powder from Everest Food Products and Laljee Godhoo and Company. These companies were found breaching FSSAI standards through subpar quality and misleading labeling. As a result, they are required to provide corrective action plans to address these violations and ensure compliance with food safety regulations.

title: From 5 days to just 2: Ex-England captain explains why Tests are getting shorter
content: Test matches are wrapping up more swiftly than they did in earlier years. The rise of aggressive T20-style batting and enhanced performances from fast bowlers are driving this trend. Additionally, the preparation of bowler-friendly pitches for the World Test Championship and the impact of DRS technology on umpiring decisions, particularly LBWs, are significant factors. Statistics reveal a noticeable increase in matches concluding within a three-day timeframe.

title: Man tied to tree, 'assaulted' by mob after visiting woman in UP; video emerges

The woman they visited was married and had recently spoken with the men. Both youths later fled the village after the incident occurred. Police registered a case against the youths for alleged abduction attempts.

Authorities have registered a case and arrested the suspect.

The squad's immediate goal is to capture gold at the Asian Games, securing their spot in the Los Angeles Olympics.

title: Centre finalising Article 371 framework for Ladakh, says Rijiju
content: ladakh is poised for a bespoke constitutional shield, says the union minister . PM Narendra Modi will visit to share his views on the proposed framework with people, the minister says . a special provision for ladka under Article 371 is going to take shape with the blessings of pm Narendra modi . the framework provides special, temporary and transitional provisions .

title: Nepal floods: MEA says 88 Indians rescued, 287 still missing
content: 88 Indian nationals have been rescued so far, while 287 remain missing . death toll from the floods has risen to 669 . forensic experts from india are expected to reach Kathmandu . teams will help in analysing DNA samples for identification of mortal remains .

title: Pak drones, armed men spur searches in Poonch, Rajouri
content: security forces launch joint cordon-and-search operations along the LoC . suspected Pakistani drones hovered in forested belts of Udhampur-Kathua and Rajouri . one drone was spotted hovering over forward areas, prompting searches early Saturday .

title: From caste & salary to 'vibe check': How India's marriage biodata is evolving
content: every year, India records approximately 10 million marriages a year . the biodata is a snapshot of a changing India, reflecting what families still look for . for women, descriptions such as “fair”, “homely” and “well-mannered” were not unusual .

title: Clash over quotas: Paswan, Manjhi trade barbs, demand each other's resignation
content: two cabinet ministers in the government sparred over reservation . they sought each other's resignation . the controversy began after awam morcha's son sought a review of the quota policy . he supported the sub-categorisation of the Scheduled Castes .

title: From society to politics: Bhagwat lays out RSS route to change
content: Bhagwat said the RSS wanted to influence policies, prevent conflicts and “stop wars” but could not begin by seeking political influence . the RSS chief said public opinion was the starting point for lasting change . he argued change must start in society and create a public view that governments cannot disregard .
